meta.title: About us | 45+ years of history — Saladín Industria Gráfica
meta.description: Founded in 1979 by Eduardo Saladín Zacarías, Saladín Industria Gráfica grew from a garage with 3 employees into 3 plants, 120 employees and the Dominican Republic's litho-lamination pioneer.

hero.title: From the garage to the free trade zone
hero.subtitle: In 1979, Eduardo Saladín Zacarías began making folding cartons with 3 employees from his home garage. Today we are an industrial printer with 3 plants, 120 employees and the country's first litho-laminated corrugated operation.

milestones.title: Founded
milestones.text: Eduardo Saladín Zacarías founds the company in the folding-carton business, with 3 employees, from his home garage.

milestones.title: The big brands arrive
milestones.text: Nestlé, Colgate, Ray-o-Vac (Spectrum Brands), Unilever and Kimberly-Clark join the client roster. Multinational standards shape our own.

milestones.title: Colgate alliance
milestones.text: We sign a strategic alliance with Colgate, a milestone that consolidates our position in folding cartons.

milestones.title: Acquisition and a new course
milestones.text: We fully acquire the folding-carton division. From 1998 to 2009 we also focus on commercial and editorial printing.

milestones.title: Reinvesting in cartons
milestones.text: We double down on folding cartons, modernizing capabilities and processes.

milestones.title: SPACK and litho-lamination
milestones.text: We expand into the Las Américas Free Trade Zone industrial park to produce high-quality litho-laminated packaging. SPACK, our export packaging brand, is born.

mission.title: Turning vision into value
mission.text: We create high-quality graphic communications, delivered on time, with great attention to detail and customer service. Our objective is to manufacture solutions that transcend the physical product: goods that add value to your brand and create a lasting connection with your customer.
mission.valuesLead: At the heart of everything we do
mission.quote: “A good name is more desirable than great riches” — Prov. 22:1
